raw_response:
I am still planting cotton this year on all 7 mu. I have done cotton many years, and on this land I know roughly how it behaves. I do not want to gamble too much. If I cut fertilizer too hard, the plants stay weak and the bolls are fewer. If I spend too much at the start, then there is no cash left if insects come or the well water costs more. So I will do it the usual way, with a moderate input level, not the biggest. I will plant after the soil warms in late April, use the cotton seed people around here commonly buy, put most fertilizer before planting, then add a smaller topdress later when the plants are growing fast. Since I have well irrigation, I will keep it for the important times, but I will not water too many times because pumping costs money. For pests, I will not spray blindly. I will watch the field and spray when I see aphids or bollworms getting serious. Family labor is limited because some people work outside, so I will keep the management simple and steady.
